---
title: "Lab 4 - Mincer Wage Regression"
output: html_document
date: "2026-10-01"
---

```{r}
# ============================================================
# LAB 4 - MINCER WAGE REGRESSION
# Race, Education, Age, Gender, Hispanic Status, and Income
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD PACKAGES
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(AER)

# If "scales" is not installed, run this ONCE in the Console:
# install.packages("scales")

library(scales)


# ============================================================
# 2. LOAD THE HOUSEHOLD PULSE DATA
# ============================================================

# OPTION 1:
# This lets you manually select d_HHP2020_241.Rdata.
# This is the safest option if R cannot find the file.

load(file.choose())

# After the window opens, select:
# d_HHP2020_241.Rdata


# ============================================================
# 3. CREATE PRIME-AGE LABOR FORCE SAMPLE
# ============================================================

prime_age_laborforce_data <- d_HHP2020_24 %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(work_kind),
    Age >= 25,
    Age <= 55,
    income_midpoint > 0
  )


# ============================================================
# 4. CHECK THE DATA
# ============================================================

summary(prime_age_laborforce_data)

summary(prime_age_laborforce_data$Age)

summary(prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint)


# ============================================================
# 5. BASIC CROSSTABS
# ============================================================

table(prime_age_laborforce_data$Education)

table(prime_age_laborforce_data$Gender)

table(prime_age_laborforce_data$Race)

table(prime_age_laborforce_data$Hispanic)

table(
  prime_age_laborforce_data$Education,
  prime_age_laborforce_data$Race
)


# ============================================================
# 6. MEAN INCOME BY EDUCATION
# ============================================================

mean_income_education <- prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  group_by(Education) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Income = mean(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Make income easier to read
mean_income_education_table <- mean_income_education %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Income = dollar(Mean_Income)
  )

print(mean_income_education_table)


# ============================================================
# 7. MEAN INCOME BY RACE
# ============================================================

mean_income_race <- prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  group_by(Race) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Income = mean(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mean_income_race_table <- mean_income_race %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Income = dollar(Mean_Income)
  )

print(mean_income_race_table)


# ============================================================
# 8. GRAPH: MEAN INCOME BY RACE
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  mean_income_race,
  aes(
    x = Race,
    y = Mean_Income,
    fill = Race
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.7,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.08)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Income by Race",
    subtitle = "Prime-Age Workers, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Race",
    y = "Mean Income"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 9. MEAN INCOME BY RACE AND EDUCATION
# ============================================================

mean_income_race_education <-
  prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  group_by(
    Race,
    Education
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Income = mean(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mean_income_race_education_table <-
  mean_income_race_education %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Income = dollar(Mean_Income)
  )

print(mean_income_race_education_table)


# ============================================================
# 10. GRAPH: RACE + EDUCATION
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  mean_income_race_education,
  aes(
    x = Education,
    y = Mean_Income,
    fill = Race
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.8
    ),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.08)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Income by Race and Education",
    subtitle = "Prime-Age Workers, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Education Level",
    y = "Mean Income",
    fill = "Race"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 35,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 11. MEAN INCOME BY RACE AND AGE
# ============================================================

mean_income_age_race <-
  prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  group_by(
    Age,
    Race
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Income = mean(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ============================================================
# 12. GRAPH: RACE + AGE
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  mean_income_age_race,
  aes(
    x = Age,
    y = Mean_Income,
    color = Race
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Income by Age and Race",
    subtitle = "Prime-Age Workers, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Mean Income",
    color = "Race"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 13. MEAN INCOME BY RACE AND GENDER
# ============================================================

mean_income_race_gender <-
  prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  group_by(
    Race,
    Gender
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Income = mean(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mean_income_race_gender_table <-
  mean_income_race_gender %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Income = dollar(Mean_Income)
  )

print(mean_income_race_gender_table)


# ============================================================
# 14. GRAPH: RACE + GENDER
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  mean_income_race_gender,
  aes(
    x = Race,
    y = Mean_Income,
    fill = Gender
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = "dodge",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.08)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Income by Race and Gender",
    subtitle = "Prime-Age Workers, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Race",
    y = "Mean Income",
    fill = "Gender"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 15. MEAN INCOME BY RACE AND HISPANIC STATUS
# ============================================================

mean_income_race_hispanic <-
  prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  group_by(
    Race,
    Hispanic
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Income = mean(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mean_income_race_hispanic_table <-
  mean_income_race_hispanic %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Income = dollar(Mean_Income)
  )

print(mean_income_race_hispanic_table)


# ============================================================
# 16. GRAPH: RACE + HISPANIC STATUS
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  mean_income_race_hispanic,
  aes(
    x = Race,
    y = Mean_Income,
    fill = Hispanic
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = "dodge",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.08)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Income by Race and Hispanic Status",
    subtitle = "Prime-Age Workers, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Race",
    y = "Mean Income",
    fill = "Hispanic Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 17. MAIN LINEAR REGRESSION
# ============================================================

model_1 <- lm(
  income_midpoint ~
    Age +
    Gender +
    Education +
    Race +
    Hispanic,
  data = prime_age_laborforce_data
)

summary(model_1)


# ============================================================
# 18. CONFIDENCE INTERVALS
# ============================================================

confint(model_1)


# ============================================================
# 19. CLASSICAL STANDARD ERRORS
# ============================================================

coeftest(model_1)


# ============================================================
# 20. ROBUST STANDARD ERRORS
# ============================================================

coeftest(
  model_1,
  vcov = vcovHC(
    model_1,
    type = "HC1"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 21. PREDICTED VALUES:
# BLACK HISPANIC FEMALE WITH ADVANCED DEGREE
# ============================================================

to_be_predicted1 <- data.frame(
  Age = 25:55,
  Gender = "female",
  Education = "adv degree",
  Race = "Black",
  Hispanic = "Hispanic"
)

to_be_predicted1$yhat <- predict(
  model_1,
  newdata = to_be_predicted1
)


# ============================================================
# 22. PREDICTED VALUES:
# SAME PROFILE WITH HIGH SCHOOL EDUCATION
# ============================================================

to_be_predicted2 <- data.frame(
  Age = 25:55,
  Gender = "female",
  Education = "high school",
  Race = "Black",
  Hispanic = "Hispanic"
)

to_be_predicted2$yhat <- predict(
  model_1,
  newdata = to_be_predicted2
)


# ============================================================
# 23. COMBINE PREDICTIONS
# ============================================================

prediction_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    Age = to_be_predicted1$Age,
    Predicted_Income = to_be_predicted1$yhat,
    Education = "Advanced Degree"
  ),
  data.frame(
    Age = to_be_predicted2$Age,
    Predicted_Income = to_be_predicted2$yhat,
    Education = "High School"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 24. GRAPH: PREDICTED INCOME
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  prediction_data,
  aes(
    x = Age,
    y = Predicted_Income,
    color = Education,
    linetype = Education
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Income by Age and Education",
    subtitle = "Black Hispanic Female, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Predicted Income",
    color = "Education",
    linetype = "Education"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 25. LOG-INCOME REGRESSION
# ============================================================

model_log <- lm(
  log(income_midpoint) ~
    Age +
    Gender +
    Education +
    Race +
    Hispanic,
  data = prime_age_laborforce_data
)

summary(model_log)


# ============================================================
# 26. COMPARE LEVEL AND LOG MODEL PREDICTIONS
# ============================================================

predicted_level <- predict(
  model_1
)

predicted_log <- predict(
  model_log
)

predicted_log_income <- exp(
  predicted_log
)

comparison <- data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Actual Mean Income",
    "Mean Predicted Income - Level Model",
    "Mean Predicted Income - Log Model"
  ),
  Mean_Income = c(
    mean(
      prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean(
      predicted_level,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean(
      predicted_log_income,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
)

comparison_table <- comparison %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Income = dollar(
      Mean_Income
    )
  )

print(comparison_table)


# ============================================================
# 27. REGRESSION WITH AGE SQUARED
# ============================================================

model_age_squared <- lm(
  income_midpoint ~
    Age +
    I(Age^2) +
    Gender +
    Education +
    Race +
    Hispanic,
  data = prime_age_laborforce_data
)

summary(model_age_squared)


# ============================================================
# 28. FINAL MODEL COMPARISON
# ============================================================

cat(
  "\n\n==============================\n",
  "LEVEL MODEL\n",
  "==============================\n"
)

print(
  summary(model_1)
)

cat(
  "\n\n==============================\n",
  "LOG-INCOME MODEL\n",
  "==============================\n"
)

print(
  summary(model_log)
)

cat(
  "\n\n==============================\n",
  "AGE-SQUARED MODEL\n",
  "==============================\n"
)

print(
  summary(model_age_squared)
)
```
